title.source: Section check: Buildings, belief and shared places
title.back: Section check: Buildings, belief and shared spaces

intro.source: 10 questions about Lessons 6–10. Take your time. You can look back at the lessons and try again as often as you like.
intro.back: 10 questions about Lessons 6–10. No need to hurry. You can go back to the lessons and try again as many times as you like.

questions.0.question.source: The posts and beams of a tongkonan are part of its structure. What does structure mean?
questions.0.question.back: The posts and beams of a tongkonan are part of its structure. What does structure mean?

questions.0.options.0.text.source: The parts that hold a building up
questions.0.options.0.text.back: The parts that hold a building up

questions.0.options.0.feedback.source: Yes. The structure is the parts that hold a building up, and how they fit together.
questions.0.options.0.feedback.back: Correct. The structure is the parts that hold a building up, and how those parts fit together.

questions.0.options.1.text.source: The carved designs on the front walls
questions.0.options.1.text.back: The carved designs on the front walls

questions.0.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. Carved designs are ornament. The structure is the posts and frame that hold the house up. Look back at Lesson 6.
questions.0.options.1.feedback.back: Not quite. Carved designs are ornament. The structure is the posts and frame that hold the house up. Go back to Lesson 6.

questions.0.options.2.text.source: The open space where people meet
questions.0.options.2.text.back: The open space where people meet

questions.0.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. The open space is between the buildings. The structure holds a building up. Look back at Lesson 6.
questions.0.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. The open space is between the buildings, while the structure holds a building up. Go back to Lesson 6.

questions.1.question.source: Look at the two photos of Toraja houses. Which question can they help you answer?
questions.1.question.back: Look at the two photos of Toraja houses. Which question can these photos help you answer?

questions.1.options.0.text.source: Who lived in each room of the house?
questions.1.options.0.text.back: Who lived in which room of the house?

questions.1.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. The photos show the outside. They do not show who lived in each room. Look back at Lesson 6.
questions.1.options.0.feedback.back: Not quite. The photos show the outside. They do not show who lived in which room. Go back to Lesson 6.

questions.1.options.1.text.source: What do all Toraja people believe today?
questions.1.options.1.text.back: What do all Toraja people believe today?

questions.1.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. A photo of a building cannot show what a whole community believes. Look back at Lesson 6.
questions.1.options.1.feedback.back: Not quite. A photo of a building cannot show what a whole community believes. Go back to Lesson 6.

questions.1.options.2.text.source: What shape are the roofs and posts?
questions.1.options.2.text.back: What shape are the roofs and posts?

questions.1.options.2.feedback.source: Yes. We can see the roofs, posts and repeated shapes. We can also see how the houses stand together.
questions.1.options.2.feedback.back: Correct. We can see the roofs, posts and repeated shapes. We can also see how the houses stand together.

questions.2.question.source: Borobudur's walls have many reliefs. What is a relief?
questions.2.question.back: Borobudur's walls have many reliefs. What is a relief?

questions.2.options.0.text.source: A long walkway that goes around a building
questions.2.options.0.text.back: A long walkway that goes around a building

questions.2.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. A long walkway is a gallery. The reliefs are the carvings on its walls. Look back at Lesson 7.
questions.2.options.0.feedback.back: Not quite. A long walkway is a gallery, while the reliefs are the carvings on its walls. Go back to Lesson 7.

questions.2.options.1.text.source: A carving that stands out from a wall
questions.2.options.1.text.back: A carving that stands out from a wall

questions.2.options.1.feedback.source: Yes. A relief stands out from a flat background. At Borobudur, reliefs tell stories in stone.
questions.2.options.1.feedback.back: Correct. A relief stands out from a flat background. At Borobudur, reliefs tell stories in stone.

questions.2.options.2.text.source: A journey to a place that is holy
questions.2.options.2.text.back: A journey to a sacred place

questions.2.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. A journey to a holy place is a pilgrimage. A relief is a kind of carving. Look back at Lesson 7.
questions.2.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. A journey to a sacred place is a pilgrimage. A relief is a kind of carving. Go back to Lesson 7.

questions.3.question.source: How did Borobudur's design guide the way people moved through it?
questions.3.question.back: How did Borobudur's design guide the way people moved?

questions.3.options.0.text.source: People walked past carved stories, then climbed up.
questions.3.options.0.text.back: People walked past carved stories, then went up

questions.3.options.0.feedback.source: Yes. People walked around the galleries past the reliefs. Then they climbed towards the top terraces.
questions.3.options.0.feedback.back: Correct. People walked around the galleries past the reliefs, then climbed up to the upper terraces.

questions.3.options.1.text.source: People stayed in one dark room in the middle.
questions.3.options.1.text.back: People stayed in one dark room in the middle

questions.3.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. Borobudur has terraces and walkways that rise to the top. People moved through it. Look back at Lesson 7.
questions.3.options.1.feedback.back: Not quite. Borobudur has terraces and walkways that rise to the top. People moved through this monument. Go back to Lesson 7.

questions.3.options.2.text.source: People only looked at it from far across the valley.
questions.3.options.2.text.back: Only looked at it from far across the valley

questions.3.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. People walked around its galleries and climbed its levels. Look back at Lesson 7.
questions.3.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. People walked around its galleries and climbed its levels. Go back to Lesson 7.

questions.4.question.source: The lesson says Angkor Wat's moat did not need to have only one purpose. Why?
questions.4.question.back: The lesson says Angkor Wat's moat did not need to have only one purpose. Why?

questions.4.options.0.text.source: It was dug long after the temple.
questions.4.options.0.text.back: It was dug long after the temple was built

questions.4.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. The moat is part of the temple's plan. It helps make the temple a picture of a universe. Look back at Lesson 8.
questions.4.options.0.feedback.back: Not quite. The moat is part of the temple's plan. It helps make the temple a picture of a universe. Go back to Lesson 8.

questions.4.options.1.text.source: It was only there to make it look pretty.
questions.4.options.1.text.back: It was there only to look beautiful

questions.4.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. The moat had meaning, and the land around it had water works for farming. Look back at Lesson 8.
questions.4.options.1.feedback.back: Not quite. The moat had meaning, and the land around it had water works for farming. Go back to Lesson 8.

questions.4.options.2.text.source: It could be sacred and useful too.
questions.4.options.2.text.back: It was sacred and useful at once

questions.4.options.2.feedback.source: Yes. The moat helped show a sacred universe. It also sat in a landscape of canals and water works.
questions.4.options.2.feedback.back: Correct. The moat helped show a sacred universe, and it also sat in a landscape of canals and water works.

questions.5.question.source: Words carved at Angkor Wat from the 1500s to the 1700s tell of pilgrims' visits. What do they show?
questions.5.question.back: Words carved at Angkor Wat from the 1500s to the 1700s tell of pilgrims' visits. What do these words show?

questions.5.options.0.text.source: The temple was first built in the 1500s.
questions.5.options.0.text.back: The temple was first built in the 1500s

questions.5.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. Angkor Wat was built in the 1100s. The carved words came much later. Look back at Lesson 8.
questions.5.options.0.feedback.note: "the 1500s to the 1700s" is ช่วงปี 1500 กว่าถึงปี 1700 กว่า, as in AAS08; "the 1100s" is ช่วงปี 1100 ถึง 1199, as in AAS08.
questions.5.options.0.feedback.back: Not quite. Angkor Wat was built between 1100 and 1199. The carved words came much later. Go back to Lesson 8.

questions.5.options.1.text.source: Later people gave the temple new meaning.
questions.5.options.1.text.back: Later people gave the temple a new meaning

questions.5.options.1.feedback.source: Yes. The temple became a Buddhist holy place. Pilgrims, some of them royal, came to pray there.
questions.5.options.1.feedback.back: Correct. The temple became a Buddhist holy place. Pilgrims, some of them royal, came to pray there.

questions.5.options.2.text.source: Every part changed religion on one date.
questions.5.options.2.text.back: Every part changed religion on one day

questions.5.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. The change was a long process. It did not happen on one single date. Look back at Lesson 8.
questions.5.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. This change took a long time. It did not happen on any single day. Go back to Lesson 8.

questions.6.question.source: What does an airwell do in a long shophouse?
questions.6.question.back: What does an airwell do in a long shophouse?

questions.6.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. That is the five-foot way, a covered path along the front. Look back at Lesson 9.
questions.6.options.0.feedback.back: Not quite. That is the five-foot way, a covered path along the front. Go back to Lesson 9.

questions.6.options.1.text.source: It brings in light and fresh air.
questions.6.options.1.text.back: It brings in light and fresh air

questions.6.options.1.feedback.source: Yes. An airwell is an open space inside. It brings light and air into deep rooms.
questions.6.options.1.feedback.back: Correct. An airwell is an open space inside. It brings light and air into deep rooms.

questions.6.options.2.text.source: It stores water for the shop below.
questions.6.options.2.text.back: It stores water for the shop below

questions.6.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. An airwell is an open space that lets in light and fresh air. Look back at Lesson 9.
questions.6.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. An airwell is an open space that lets in light and fresh air. Go back to Lesson 9.

questions.7.stimulus.title.source: A made-up photo of a made-up port
questions.7.stimulus.title.back: A made-up photo of a made-up port

questions.7.stimulus.body.source: This is a made-up example. A photo shows a row of grand houses beside a canal in the made-up port of Velmar. The houses are tall and made of brick. Their fronts are clean and decorated.
questions.7.stimulus.body.back: This is a made-up example. A photo shows a row of grand houses beside a canal in the port of Velmar, a made-up town. These houses are tall and built of brick. Their fronts are clean and decorated.

questions.7.question.source: Which question would need other sources, such as city records?
questions.7.question.back: Which question would need other sources, such as city records?

questions.7.options.0.text.source: How was each house paid for?
questions.7.options.0.text.back: Where did the money for each house come from?

questions.7.options.0.feedback.source: Yes. A street view cannot show where the money came from. Records can tell us more.
questions.7.options.0.feedback.back: Correct. A street view cannot show where the money came from. Records can tell us more.

questions.7.options.1.text.source: What are the houses made of?
questions.7.options.1.text.back: What are these houses built of?

questions.7.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. You can see in the photo that the houses are brick. Look back at Lesson 9.
questions.7.options.1.feedback.back: Not quite. You can see in the photo that the houses are built of brick. Go back to Lesson 9.

questions.7.options.2.text.source: Do the houses stand by a canal?
questions.7.options.2.text.back: Do these houses stand beside a canal?

questions.7.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. The photo shows the canal. You need records for what a photo cannot show. Look back at Lesson 9.
questions.7.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. The photo shows the canal. You need records for what a photo cannot show. Go back to Lesson 9.

questions.8.question.source: In Ifugao, each family owns its own fields. Why do families also work as a team?
questions.8.question.back: In Ifugao, each family owns its own fields. Why do families also work together as a team?

questions.8.options.0.text.source: Every field belongs to the whole village.
questions.8.options.0.text.back: Every field belongs to the whole village

questions.8.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. Each household owns its own terraces. Shared work does not mean shared fields. Look back at Lesson 10.
questions.8.options.0.feedback.back: Not quite. Each household owns its own terraces. Working together does not mean the fields are shared. Go back to Lesson 10.

questions.8.options.1.text.source: Only one family knows how to grow rice.
questions.8.options.1.text.back: Only one family knows how to grow rice

questions.8.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. Many people pass on knowledge about seeds, soil and water. Look back at Lesson 10.
questions.8.options.1.feedback.back: Not quite. Many people pass on knowledge about seeds, soil and water. Go back to Lesson 10.

questions.8.options.2.text.source: Walls and water need shared care.
questions.8.options.2.text.back: Walls and water need shared care

questions.8.options.2.feedback.source: Yes. Walls and water systems link the fields. So each household depends on its neighbours.
questions.8.options.2.feedback.back: Correct. Walls and water systems link the fields together, so each household depends on its neighbours.

questions.9.stimulus.body.source: This is a made-up example. In the made-up valley of Orun, farmers grow rice on terraces. A small wood grows above the terraces. One year, people cut down most of the trees. After that, the water reaching the fields was hard to control.
questions.9.stimulus.body.back: This is a made-up example. In Orun, a made-up valley, farmers grow rice on terraces. There is a small wood above the terraces. One year, people cut down almost all the trees. After that, the water flowing down to the fields was hard to control.

questions.9.question.source: Which idea from Lesson 10 helps explain what happened in Orun?
questions.9.question.back: Which idea from Lesson 10 helps explain what happened in Orun?

questions.9.options.0.text.source: Woods above terraces help control water.
questions.9.options.0.text.back: Woods above terraces help control water

questions.9.options.0.feedback.source: Yes. Small woods above the terraces help control the water that reaches the fields.
questions.9.options.0.feedback.back: Correct. Small woods above the terraces help control the water that reaches the fields.

questions.9.options.1.text.source: Terraces need no care once they are built.
questions.9.options.1.text.back: Terraces need no care once they are built

questions.9.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. Fields, walls and water need care all the time. Look back at Lesson 10.
questions.9.options.1.feedback.back: Not quite. Fields, walls and water need care all the time. Go back to Lesson 10.

questions.9.options.2.text.source: A terrace is only a pretty pattern on a hill.
questions.9.options.2.text.back: A terrace is only a pretty pattern on a hill

questions.9.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. Terraces are farming work. Land, walls, water and woods are all linked. Look back at Lesson 10.
questions.9.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. Terraces are farming work. Land, walls, water and woods are all linked. Go back to Lesson 10.

results.high.back: Well done. You know a lot about how buildings and places affect people's lives.

results.middle.source: Good work. You remember many of the main ideas. Look back at any lesson you want to check.
results.middle.back: Good work. You remember many of the main ideas. Go back to any lesson you want to review.

results.low.back: Thank you for trying. Go back to Lessons 6–10, then try again whenever you like.
